simple.meaning: גַּבַּחַת (gabbachath) is a Hebrew object word meaning “baldness in the forehead; by analogy, a bare spot on the right side of cloth.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Leviticus 13:42. The surrounding context includes kingship, priesthood.

definitions.short: baldness in the forehead; by analogy, a bare spot on the right side of cloth
definitions.full: H1372. gabbachath גַּבַּ֫חַת noun feminine bald forehead (Late Hebrew id. , Aramaic ), only Leviticus 13 — absolute Lev 13:42 (P; asson. בַגַּבַּ֫חַת אוֺ בְּקָרַ֫חַת ); גַּבַּחְתּוֺ 13:42 ; 13:43 (both P & || קָרַחְתּוֺ ); in all, as place of appearance of an eruption; 13:55 (P; || id.) = in its front , i.e. front of garment. גֹּבַי see below גבה . סַלָּ֑י גַּבַּי גַּבַּי, see below גבב .

occurrences.englishText: But if a reddish-white plague is in the bald head or the bald forehead, it is leprosy breaking out in his bald head or his bald forehead.
But if a reddish-white plague is in the bald head or the bald forehead, it is leprosy breaking out in his bald head or his bald forehead.
Then the priest shall examine him. Behold, if the swelling of the plague is reddish-white in his bald head, or in his bald forehead, like the appearance of leprosy in the skin of the body,

Then the priest shall examine it, after the plague is washed; and behold, if the plague hasn’t changed its color, and the plague hasn’t spread, it is unclean; you shall burn it in the fire. It is a mildewed spot, whether the bareness is inside or outside.
